newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended the session on Monday slightly lower, pulled down by blue chip companies including ONA Group, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 429.12 points from 429.43 points.
CFG 25 Index CFG 25.CS, which tracks the 25 most liquid stocks, closed at 6,845.73 points, down 0.18 from last week.
ONA Group, which holds stakes in more than 100 companies, lost 10 dirhams to close at 440 dirhams.
The group, with a market capitalisation of more than 7.7 billion dirhams, was among the blue chips which drove the market higher last week.
"The main contributors to the bourse index decline were ONA Group and BMCE bank," a stockbroker at Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) said.
"At present, the market has reached its equilibrium level...It also became liquid for blue chip companies," he said.
He named these as BMCE, which lost five dirhams to close at 420, Wafabank, Banque Commerciale du Maroc and Sonsid steel mill.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant, remained unchanged at 247 dirhams.
Wafabank, one of the main market capitalisations, remained also unchanged at 503 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the bourse's largest capitalisation, remained unchanged at 740 dirhams, analysts said.
The bourse traded volume was 16 million dirhams on the official market and 2.3 million on the over-the-counter market, CFI said.
